headline: Ducks’ Troy Terry expected to make season debut Wednesday
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Ducks forward Troy Terry is expected to make his season debut Wednesday against the Predators, with head coach Joel Quenneville saying Terry will "likely" be in the lineup.

Anaheim has managed without him, going 10-7-1 for 21 points through 18 games, but the underlying numbers say that record is flattering. The Ducks have created 48% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, and only 45% at five-on-five. They've scored 10.7 more goals than expected, which usually doesn't last. Their power play is generating 0.76 expected goals per game, the same as Nashville's, so Terry's return doesn't change much there on paper. Even so, a lineup that has leaned on finishing luck could use more real chance creation at even strength, which is where he can help. Nashville sits level on 21 points but with the opposite profile: 49.9% of expected goals, 3.5 fewer goals than expected, and a goalie group saving 6.7 goals above expected. That makes it a fair test for a Ducks team still looking for more sustainable results.
